get.description:
Every knob an operator may change, with its current effective value.

Built from the settable set, so a credential, a DSN or a frozen identifier cannot appear here
even by accident — the filter is in one place rather than repeated per field.

schema.title: Response Effective Config Api V1 App Operator Config Get

put.description: Override one policy value. Refused if the boot guard would refuse it.

schema.title: Response Set Config Api V1 App Operator Config Put

delete.description: Drop an override so the configured default applies again.

get.description:
Every commerce option this service gates, with its effective enabled/locked state for a scope.

A self-serve UI reads `locked` to know an option is frozen (grey the toggle out); `source` says
whether a stored override or the built-in default decided it.

schema.title: Response List Options Api V1 App Operator Options Get

put.description: Enable/disable (and optionally lock) one commerce option for a scope.

schema.title: Response Set Option Api V1 App Operator Options Put

delete.description: Drop an option override so it resolves to its default again.

schema.title: Response Clear Option Api V1 App Operator Options  Option  Delete

get.description:
Which credentials are set, and a four-character hint for each.

There is no value in this response and no route that would return one. The hint exists so an
operator can tell which key is loaded before replacing it — replacing the wrong one is the
mistake this prevents.

schema.title: Response List Secrets Api V1 App Operator Secrets Get

put.description:
Set or rotate a credential. The previous one stays valid for a bounded window.

Audited BEFORE the write: a change the log cannot take must not happen, and here the old value
is overwritten by the action itself, so an unrecorded rotation is unreconstructable.

schema.title: Response Set Secret Api V1 App Operator Secrets Put

delete.description: Remove a credential so the configured environment value applies again.

schema.title: Response Clear Secret Api V1 App Operator Secrets  Name  Delete

get.description:
302 the customer to the gateway's hosted page for this request — or refuse (unknown, expired,
spent, or a target host that is not allow-listed). NO EXISTENCE ORACLE (audit FIN-013): an unknown
id and an existing-but-unusable one return the IDENTICAL response (404 + one generic body), so a
link holder cannot tell 'never existed' from 'exists but spent/expired'. Only the happy path (a
live, allow-listed link) differs — it 302s. Never redirects to an unvetted host.

post.description:
Receive the marketplace provider's payout/settlement webhook. No token (the provider has none of
ours); the handler re-queries the provider for the payout (verify-by-fetch) and applies it
idempotently, so a forged/replayed POST settles nothing. Always 200 to a well-formed request so the
provider does not retry-storm; 503 only when the provider is unreachable (verification pending).

Receive a shop gateway's status webhook. The tenant in the path selects whose gateway verifies
it; verification (signature / verify-by-fetch) is the gate, and application is idempotent, so a
forged or replayed POST changes nothing. Always 200 to a well-formed request so the gateway does
not retry-storm; the body says whether anything was applied.

schema.title: Response Whoami Api V1 Whoami Get

post.description:
Produce a sealed, checksummed archive of this service's declared data.

Called by backup-service, on a schedule, over the internal token. What this service holds is
declared in app/backup_manifest.py; how it is read lives in core/backup.py. The orchestrator
stores the archive and never sees the plaintext.

schema.title: Response Backup Export Internal Backup Export Post

post.description: Restore an archive this service produced. Idempotent; leaves newer rows alone by default.

schema.title: Response Backup Import Internal Backup Import Post

post.description:
Prove an archive restores, by test-restoring it into a throwaway namespace and comparing.

backup-service calls this after it stores an archive (passing back the bytes it read FROM the
store, so corruption at rest is caught too). This service is the only party that can unseal its
own archive and knows its own schema, so verification lives here; the orchestrator only records
the verdict. The throwaway namespace is torn down before this returns — nothing is left behind,
and live data is never touched.

schema.title: Response Backup Verify Internal Backup Verify Post

post.description:
Record (or update) a tenant's sub-merchant destination id + status — used by the hosted-onboarding
callback once the provider approves, or by an operator. Stores only the opaque provider id.

schema.title: Response Set Submerchant Destination Internal Payments Sub Merchants Destination Post

post.description:
Register a tenant as a sub-merchant of the platform's marketplace provider. `api` forwards the KYB
data to the provider and stores ONLY the returned destination id; `hosted` returns a handle for the
client-side flow (the destination arrives later via /sub-merchants/destination). The PROVIDER does the
KYC; we never store the IBAN/documents. Write-ahead audited (it decides where a shop's money goes).

schema.title: Response Onboard Submerchant Internal Payments Sub Merchants Onboard Post

get.description:
The tenant's sub-merchant status + destination id (an opaque provider id, safe for an internal
caller). No bank details are ever stored, so none can be returned.

schema.title: Response Get Submerchant Internal Payments Sub Merchants  Tenant  Get

post.description:
Erase a data subject. Called by compliance-service during a DSAR fan-out.

Returns the ack: what was erased, and what was RETAINED with its legal basis. Idempotent — a
DSAR retries, so erasing an already-erased subject must not fail. Wire this service into the
fan-out by adding it to PRIVACY_TARGETS in compliance-service's values file; the
safety:privacy-wiring gate fails if you implement this and forget.

schema.title: Response Erase Subject Internal Privacy Erase Post
